subject: Budget velocity check — pilot vs scale spend windows & PO lead time
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Morales <elena@orchardapps.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Oct 2027 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Budget velocity check — pilot vs scale spend windows & PO lead time

Hi Elena — thanks again for your time this morning. Quick recap + the pricing materials attached so your procurement team can review.

Summary of what we discussed (pricing/units callouts):
- Token profiles we saw on the call: short-chat bursts (median 120 tokens), summaries ~6–8k tokens/session, embeddings batch jobs ~500k tokens/day.
- Pilot band (recommended initial test): $15k–$25k / month — roughly 8–12M tokens/mo. Good for a 6–8 week pilot with throughput testing.
- Scale band (typical mid-stage): $60k–$120k / month — ~40–80M tokens/mo; includes standard batching and KV-cache configs to reduce unit cost.
- Enterprise band: $250k+ / month — optimized routing, quantized variants, and SLA-backed pools for latency-sensitive traffic.

Procurement/approval heuristics we flagged:
- PO requirement: Orchard indicated POs for vendor spend > $25k/mo. If that holds, pilot sits right at the PO threshold — expect a shorter lead time if we structure as a short-term pilot/credit.
- Finance lead time: estimate 4–8 weeks depending on PO size and legal review; >$100k could add 6–10 weeks.

Unit economics examples (ballpark, list price):
- 1M tokens: $2,200 / $/1M
- 10M tokens: $1,600 / $/1M (volume discounts + batching)
- 100M tokens: $1,100 / $/1M (contracted reserved capacity and quantization recommendations applied)

Attachments: Redwood-pricing-estimate-v2.pdf (detailed banded estimate), mutual-action-plan.xlsx (roles / dates / procurement contacts).

Asks / next steps:
1) Can you confirm which monthly band you expect to target for Q1 (Pilot / Scale / Enterprise)?
2) Who on your side owns PO approvals (name + email)?
3) Any constraints on payment terms (net-30 / net-45 / prepaid)?

If helpful, we can propose a pilot structure that avoids a formal PO (prepaid credit or short-term invoice) so you can start in 1–2 weeks while procurement completes the PO.

Thanks — I attached the two files referenced above. Happy to hop on a 20-min follow-up with procurement if that moves things faster.

Best,

--
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Soojin — useful summary. A couple quick clarifying questions before I loop procurement: 

1) Does the 1M/10M/100M $/1M table you sent assume the quantized model variants (we generally prefer the smaller memory footprint for embeddings)?
2) For pilots sitting at $20–25k/month, what’s the recommended commitment (duration) to get the 10–15% pilot discount you mentioned in the call?
3) Our finance team has been pushing Net-45 for new vendors. Is Net-45 an option for Orchard at scale, or do you typically require Net-30?

If you can send a quick line item breakdown (1M/10M/100M) and a suggested pilot commitment term, I’ll forward to procurement and loop in procurement@orchardapps.com.

—Elena

Looping in with a few operational suggestions before we reply to Elena: 

- For pilots in the $15k–$25k band, offer a 90-day pilot at a 12% discount plus a one-time $5k onboarding credit. Structure as prepaid credit if the customer is flexible — this avoids PO delays and lets them start immediately.
- For Net-45: finance will accept Net-45 on a case-by-case basis for customers with an existing relationship; for new logos we prefer Net-30 but can approve Net-45 for deals >$100k ARR with a signed SOW that includes the payment term.
- PO lead time assumptions: under $100k we should plan 4–6 weeks; $100k–$250k: 6–10 weeks; >$250k: expect legal to add 8+ weeks unless we engage procurement early.

If you want, I’ll draft a 1-paragraph LOI template for them to send to procurement to accelerate approvals.

-Aditya
VP, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Wed, 20 Oct 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Budget velocity check — pilot vs scale spend windows & PO lead time

Hi Elena — quick follow-up with answers and a slightly updated estimate attached.

Answers to your questions: 
1) The $/1M numbers I shared are conservative list prices that assume standard quantized options where applicable. For embeddings we expect a ~10–20% efficiency improvement with the quantized embedding variant; I noted that in the updated estimate.
2) Pilot discount: 12% for a 90-day pilot; to qualify put a letter of intent (simple email or LOI) and an internal PO/commitment to convert to a paid plan within 90 days. If procurement needs to delay the PO, we can provide a prepaid credit option to start immediately.
3) Net-45: we can offer Net-45 for Orchard for the initial contract at scale (Finance has approved Net-45 for deals that include reserved capacity or >$100k ARR). For pilots under $50k we typically require prepaid or Net-30.

Procurement lead time guidance (updated):
- PO < $25k: often same-week to 2 weeks (rare in your case).
- PO $25k–$100k: expect 3–6 weeks (procurement + finance).
- PO $100k–$250k: 6–10 weeks (legal review likely).

Next steps I propose: 
- Elena: confirm target monthly band (Pilot / Scale / Enterprise) and share procurement contact.
- If Pilot: sign simple LOI (I can send a 1-paragraph draft) and choose prepaid credits vs PO route.
- If Scale/Enterprise: confirm target start quarter so we can provision reserved capacity and provide a more detailed unit-econ SOW and a preferred payment term in the draft contract.

Attached: Redwood-pricing-estimate-v2-updated.pdf (shows quantized variant assumptions and the pilot credit option).

Can we lock a short procurement sync on Friday for 20 minutes? If so, I’ll include Aditya and Marissa from our side.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,

--
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
